title: The Default Trap: Rethinking Plan Evaluation in Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.36829v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An executor can respond strongly to a change in a supplied plan's priority while showing a small change in the same information-selection probability when a default-aligned whole plan is removed. We call the risk of interpreting the latter as weak responsiveness to alternative priorities the default trap. We compare paired plans that prioritize different information targets with a shared no-plan reference. An accounting identity relates these distinct behavioral contrasts. Across 3,200 decision windows on 160 selected Retail, Airline, and AgentDojo tasks, switching priorities strongly redirects two models' choices, while the two plan-versus-default contrasts differ. In 2,160 additional windows, reversing account-list order shifts default target selection by 63.3-98.3 percentage points; priority-switching effects remain 96.7-100.0 points in either order. A separate 3,240-window component study finds strong control under single priority se

translated_title: 默认陷阱：重新思考工具使用型LLM智能体中的计划评估
translated_abstract: 当移除与默认对齐的完整计划时，执行器可能对所提供计划优先级的变化表现出强烈响应，而其在相同信息上的选择概率却仅发生微小变化。我们将把后者误读为对替代优先级弱响应性的风险称为“默认陷阱”。我们比较了优先不同信息目标的成对计划与共享的无计划参照，并通过一个会计恒等式将这些不同的行为对比关联起来。在160个精选的零售、航空和AgentDojo任务上的3,200个决策窗口中，切换优先级强烈地改变了两个模型的选择，而两种“计划对默认”的行为对比则存在差异。在另外2,160个窗口中，反转账户列表顺序使默认目标选择移动了63.3-98.3个百分点；而优先级切换效应在任一顺序下均保持在96.7-100.0个百分点。另一项独立的3,240个窗口的组件研究发现，在单一优先级设置下存在强控制（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出“默认陷阱”这一新概念，指出移除默认对齐计划后模型行为变化小不应被误读为对替代优先级响应弱，并通过数千个决策窗口的实验证明计划优先级切换可强烈（96.7-100.0个百分点）引导LLM智能体的选择，而“计划对默认”的行为对比会因列表顺序等因素而产生误导。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "default trap"—the risk of misinterpreting small behavioral changes after removing a default-aligned plan as weak responsiveness to alternative priorities—and demonstrates across thousands of decision windows that plan priority-switching strongly redirects LLM agents' choices (96.7-100.0 percentage points) while plan-versus-default contrasts can be misleading due to factors like list ordering.
